blogs.title: Why Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model: Demystifying Direct Preference Optimization
blogs.description: Explain in plain language what DPO is, why it eliminates the recycling of RL, and how the reward model is implicitly embedded in the language model. Use analogies like a “policy‑to‑reward” secret handshake that lets developers avoid a complex RL loop.

blogs.title: From Human Likes to Smart Responses: How Direct Preference Optimization Turns Feedback into a Better Bot
blogs.description: Walk through the practical workflow: generate completions, collect “which is better” judgments, and feed them straight into a binary cross‑entropy loss. Show how this replaces the two‑step RLHF pipeline and is easier to run on commodity hardware.

blogs.title: Scaling Down the Complexities of RLHF: The Computational Edge of DPO
blogs.description: Compare the resource demands of PPO‑based RLHF with the lightweight DPO approach. Highlight real‑world speedups, fewer hyper‑parameters, and how this opens up fine‑tuning for smaller teams or resource‑constrained labs.

blogs.title: Beyond Sentiment: DPO in Summarization, Dialogue, and More Open‑Ended Tasks
blogs.description: Present case studies from the paper—sentiment‑controlled generation, Reddit TL;DR summarization, and Anthropic’s Helpful & Harmless dialogue. Explain how DPO matches or beats PPO in win‑rate tests and why it generalises across domains.

blogs.title: Is GPT‑4 a Reliable Judge? Using Large Models as Human Feedback Proxies in DPO Training
blogs.description: Discuss the paper’s human‑in‑the‑loop validation: how GPT‑4 judgments were calibrated against real humans, what prompts matter, and what this means for future automated evaluation pipelines.
